note: The Ethics Exam rigged instrument (Room M5, THE CODE). The article text is the documented 1924 language; scenario outcomes derive from the documented expulsion rule. The exam contains no morally correct answer a member could afford, and that is its lesson.
articleText: A Realtor should never be instrumental in introducing into a neighborhood a character of property or occupancy, members of any race or nationality, or any individuals whose presence will clearly be detrimental to property values in that neighborhood.

scenarios.prompt: A Black surgeon with flawless credit offers full asking price on a white block. You hold the listing.
scenarios.sellOutcome: Expulsion proceedings under the code. The license that feeds your family is gone.
scenarios.refuseOutcome: Ethical, in the code's own terms. The sale is refused and the line holds.

scenarios.prompt: A Black schoolteacher and her husband, savings in hand, ask to see a listing two blocks past the line.
scenarios.sellOutcome: The board reads the code the same way for every member. Expulsion.
scenarios.refuseOutcome: Ethical, in the code's own terms. The family keeps looking inside the Black Belt.

debrief.heading: There was no right answer at this desk
debrief.body: The exam contained no morally correct answer a member could afford. That was its function. The code made the color line a professional duty, and a realtor who crossed it lost the livelihood that fed his family. The explicit language came out of the code in 1950. The association formally apologized in 2020.
